newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine sunoil imports may rise.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine sunoil imports may rise.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, and independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE: HIGH SUNSEED EXPORTS COULD TRIGGER SUNOIL IMPORT RISE

MOSCOW, April 17 - Total sunseed exports from October 1996 through March 1997 could total a high 860,000 tonnes out of 1996 domestic output of 2.12 million tonnes, implying that around 40 percent of total sunseed output has been exported in the first half of 1996/97 (October-September).
Almost all of the sunseeds were shipped outside the former Soviet Union.
Crushing during October 1996 - February 1997 is estimated at 575,000 tonnes, which equals 247,300 tonnes of sunoil based on an average extraction rate of 43 percent.
Due to the high sunseed exports, domestic sunoil production declined sharply to 29,000 tonnes in March 1997 from 62,000 tonnes in November 1996.
Sunseed crushing industry sources have reported further decreases in sunoil production since March, because of shortages of sunseeds.
As a result, domestic sunoil stocks declined from 4,200 tonnes in early January to an estimated 3,000 tonnes at the beginning of April.

Based on the current rate of sunoil production and domestic consumption, sunoil stocks could be depleted within the next two to three months, possibly leading to a sharp decline in sunoil exports and an increase in domestic sunoil prices.
A rise in sunoil imports is also likely, but they are restricted by a 30 percent import duty on sunoil.

However, imports may increase through swap contracts, whereby a domestic company delivers sunseeds from Ukraine and takes sunoil back to Ukraine, thereby avoiding the import duty. TABLE 1: UKRAINE MONTHLY SUNSEED AND SUNOIL EXPORTS
